question: How often do the radioactive atoms in your body split the universe?
answer: Each radioactive nucleus in your body is in a superposition of decayed and not decayed. When one decays, it hits what is around it, becomes entangled, and the universe branches. Your body has about 5,000 such decays every second.
move: Branching is constant: your own body does it thousands of times a second.

web.label: A person drawn big, the radioactive atoms in their body as yellow dots, one of them decaying: their world splits there into a copy where the atom decayed and one where it did not. The reader drags along a scale from 1 to 100,000 splits a second to guess how often this happens, then rates how sure they are.

source: Veritasium, “Why Parallel Universes Are Probably Real” (YouTube, 2020)
